title: The gentle form returns (11.47–11.55)
hook: after the thousand suns, the friend's face comes back, and Arjuna can breathe again

segments.voice: Yesterday: Arjuna's terror and praise, and a friend asking to be forgiven for every joke. Your line was forgive my familiarity. Day two hundred. Two hundred days on this path. And today, the end of chapter eleven.
screen: `ARJUNA'S TERROR AND PRAISE — FORGIVE MY FAMILIARITY.`

segments.voice: Think of a child who's had a nightmare, shaking in the dark. The parent comes in and turns on the small lamp by the bed. Same room. Same shadows in the corners. But now there's a familiar face, and a voice that says, it's okay, I'm here. The child can breathe again. Arjuna has seen the whole universe blazing in Krishna's body, mouths and fire and time itself. And he asked, please, show me the form I know. Today, Krishna does.
screen: `A NIGHTMARE IN THE DARK.` → `A SMALL LAMP, A FAMILIAR FACE.` → `SHOW ME THE FORM I KNOW.`

segments.voice: Verse forty-seven: out of grace, through my own power, I showed you this highest form, full of light, universal, infinite, first. No one but you has seen it before. Verse forty-eight: not by the Vedas, not by sacrifice, not by study, not by gifts, not by rituals, not by fierce austerities can I be seen in this form by anyone but you. Then verse forty-nine, the tender turn. Don't be afraid. Don't be bewildered by seeing this terrible form of mine. Let your fear go, be glad at heart, and see my familiar form again. Sanjaya tells what happens. Krishna shows his own form again, and, becoming gentle in form, saumya, the great soul comforts the frightened Arjuna. Saumya is a lovely word: gentle, mild, moon-like, cool after heat. Arjuna, verse fifty-one: seeing this gentle human form of yours, I'm myself again. I've come back to my nature. And then Krishna says what the whole chapter was pointing at. This form you've seen is very hard to see; even the gods long to see it. Not by Vedas, not by austerity, not by gifts or sacrifice. But by devotion alone, bhakti, undivided, can I be known like this, seen truly, and entered. And the last verse of the chapter, which some call the essence of the whole Gita: whoever works for me, holds me as the goal, is devoted to me, free of attachment, and without hatred toward any being, comes to me. Without hatred toward any being. That's today's word, the gentle form returns. After the thousand suns, the friend's face, and the way to it: by devotion alone.
screen: `NO ONE BUT YOU HAS SEEN IT.` · `DON'T BE AFRAID.` · `SAUMYA: GENTLE, MOON-LIKE.` · `WITHOUT HATRED TOWARD ANY BEING.` · then, large: `BY DEVOTION ALONE.`

segments.voice: Sit, and let yourself come down after a big week of chapters. Breathe out slowly, as if after a fright. Picture a familiar, gentle face, of God if you pray, or of someone who has comforted you. Let their presence say what Krishna said: don't be afraid. Let your shoulders drop. Stay with the gentleness, cool and quiet, like moonlight. The bell holds the time.
The gentle form returns. After the vision, Krishna takes his familiar human form again, and says he's truly seen by devotion alone.
Your line: by devotion alone. Today, be the gentle face for someone who's frightened or overwhelmed. Say, it's okay, I'm here. Day two hundred.

howItsDone: Most Hindu worship is directed to God in a gentle, familiar form, an image of Krishna, Rama, Shiva or the Goddess, and many devotees cite Gita 11.54–55 to say that loving devotion, not ritual alone, is how God is truly known.

match.prompt: what's inside the verses — tap the pairs.

myth: Krishna says study and sacrifice are enough to see this form
verses 48 and 53: not by Vedas, sacrifice, study, gifts or austerity, but by devotion alone.
Arjuna says he feels himself again when he sees the gentle form
verse 51: seeing your gentle human form, I'm myself again.
the last verse of chapter 11 includes freedom from hatred toward any being
verse 55: without enmity toward any being, the devotee comes to him.

fork.setup: Krishna says his cosmic form can't be seen by Vedas, sacrifice, study or austerity. then how can it be known?
fork.reveal: by devotion alone, verse 54: bhaktya tv ananyaya, by undivided devotion he can be known, seen, and entered.

original.note: Sanskrit: saumya, gentle, mild, moon-like; the gentle form Krishna takes again in 11.50.

trapdoor: what you thought: seeing God's full glory is the goal.
what it means: after the overwhelming vision, the gentle, familiar form returns; God is truly known by devotion alone.

what a scholar hears: commentators differ on whether 11.46–50 shows a four-armed form before the two-armed human one; 11.55 is often called the essence (sara) of the Gita by commentators such as Shankara.

notes: Whether Krishna shows a four-armed form (asked for in 11.46) before the two-armed human form (11.50–51) is debated among commentators; the script avoids deciding.
'11.55 is called the essence of the Gita' is attributed to Shankara from memory; confirm or drop the name.
